title: Hospital Account Self-Pay Final Bills — Valuation in the Medical Hardship Debt
content:
Under the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care), one account is revalued in the qualifying medical debt Riverbend documents for its own charges, and the documented debt moves by the difference between the revalued figure and the figure as posted (down when the revalued figure is lower). The revaluation never raises a bill or a share above what is posted.

**The self-pay account** is the patient's Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account carrying the patient's most recent self-pay final-bill liability (on a same-day tie, the liability listed first in the account activity). Its window postings are those for which fewer than twelve whole months separate the posting date from the documentation day, a whole month running from a day of one month to the same day of the next month or, when the next month has no such day, to the first day of the month after it. Its **bill** is its self-pay final-bill liabilities in that window less its uninsured discounts (an observation-rate discount included) and package price adjustments in that window, and its **amounts-generally-billed share** is the program's amounts-generally-billed percentage (34.6 percent on every tier) of its self-pay final-bill liabilities in that window, rounded half-up to the cent.

**The insured account** is the account of the Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing) claim carrying the patient's most recent payer payment (on a same-day tie, the payment listed first in the claim activity), when that claim is not in appealed status, that account is not on a billing hold and it is coded emergency or medically necessary. Its window postings are those for which fewer than twelve whole months separate the posting date from the documentation day, a whole month running from a day of one month to the same day of the next month or, when the next month has no such day, to the first day of the month after it. Its **patient share** is the patient liabilities posted from that claim in that window, and its **amounts-generally-billed share** is 34.6 percent of its gross charges, rounded half-up to the cent.

**Revaluation, in one of three ways.**

| Case | Revalued figure |
|---|---|
| the self-pay account is coded emergency or medically necessary and no Good Faith & Price Estimates self-pay good faith estimate (single scheduled service, procedure with co-providers or recurring course of care) whose service has been completed, which is closed or which is in dispute is linked to it | its bill is replaced by the smaller of that bill and its amounts-generally-billed share |
| no self-pay account so qualifies and an insured account exists | its patient share is replaced by the smaller of that share and its amounts-generally-billed share, a patient eligible for financial assistance being charged no more than the amounts generally billed for emergency or medically necessary care |
| otherwise | nothing is revalued |

**Worked cases (hypothetical).**
- Self-pay account, medically necessary, no linked estimate: final-bill liabilities in the window 5,000.00, uninsured discounts 2,000.00, bill 3,000.00, share 1,730.00. The bill becomes 1,730.00 and the debt moves down by 1,270.00.
- Same account with uninsured discounts of 3,500.00 (an observation-rate discount among them): bill 1,500.00, below the 1,730.00 share; nothing changes.
- Self-pay account coded elective, and an insured account with gross charges of 10,000.00 (share 3,460.00) and a patient share of 4,000.00 in the window: the patient share becomes 3,460.00 and the debt moves down by 540.00. With a patient share of 2,000.00 nothing changes.
